# Shop inventory workspace

Open Catalogue, choose Shop, then Inventory. The workspace stays pinned to the selected branch; switch branches from More before opening another workspace. No quantities are combined across measures or branches.

## Implemented flows

- Stock: server-authoritative effective physical availability, on-hand, reserved, quarantined, in-transit and backorder figures. Full-screen stock detail uses the balance endpoint, including its independent balance revision. Adjustments use that revision, never a catalogue version.
- Stock tracking: new tracking for an active branch listing. Choose a real measure, consumption mode, FIFO/FEFO and lot tracking. Approximate measures cannot be silently converted. Existing tracking is not reconfigured without a readable stock-basis version contract. If all active listings are already tracked, the setup screen explains why there are no new choices and offers Receive goods for existing tracked stock, followed by receipt review/posting. With no active listing or tracked stock, it directs the user to create or activate a Shop branch listing in Catalogue.
- Receiving: a full-screen, multi-item form selects existing stock bases, whole stock quantities, received date/time and optional delivery/supplier references, notes, lot/batch details, manufacture/best-before/expiry dates and unit cost. A saved draft opens its review screen. Posting is a separate confirmed command. Draft cancellation leaves stock unchanged. Posted reversal uses the same cancel endpoint; the backend must confirm the original lots remain intact.
- Transfers: select real source/destination stock tracking for the same variant, review and save a draft, then explicitly dispatch. Dispatch removes source on-hand and records source in-transit stock. Record arrivals incrementally with usable, damaged and missing quantities; only usable goods increase destination stock. Partial arrivals remain open until every sent unit is accounted for. Draft cancellation is available before dispatch; there is no invented approval or post-dispatch cancellation action. Full-screen detail shows the route, progress, quantities and discrepancies.
- Adjustments: a full-screen form chooses add/remove, a backend-controlled reason and an optional note. Confirm before applying. Stale revision responses reload the balance and require the user to review before submitting again.
- Stocktakes: full branch counts or selected cycle counts create a backend snapshot. Physical counts use a focused sheet; zero is valid. Post stays disabled until every returned line is counted. Stock moving after the snapshot requires a new stocktake and recount. No unsupported cancellation route is invented.
- Quarantine: a full-screen form selects actual branch stock, whole quantities and one of the six controlled Shop reasons, with an optional note. A review sheet confirms the stock hold. Quarantine keeps on-hand unchanged while excluding held units from sellable stock. Case details show quantity, reason, lifecycle and recorded dates; release and permanent disposal are visible, separately confirmed actions. These resolve the entire case, with no invented partial-release or reopen command. Release removes the hold; expired stock still stays unavailable. Disposal removes both the hold and those units from on-hand.
- Reorder rules: open a stock item and use its Reorder rule card. A focused sheet sets a non-negative minimum, a strictly higher target up to 1,000,000,000 stock units, and optional expiry warning hours from 1 to 8,760. Empty hours explicitly submit null to clear the window. Saved rules remain server authority; the card displays the returned suggested reorder quantity, which is target minus valid sellable stock, floored at zero, independently of the minimum alert threshold. Saving leaves physical stock and balance revisions unchanged and does not place orders. Saving an existing inactive or archived rule activates it, as the backend upsert specifies; the card and editing sheet explain this state change. No unsupported delete, pause, supplier or purchase action is invented.
- History: paginated branch movements with a detail sheet, including physical and reservation/quarantine/transit deltas, source and timestamps.
- Alerts: paginated branch alerts with details, acknowledgment and resolution. These actions change alert state, not stock.

## Mock and Live

Mock remains the app default. Fixtures reference the same catalogue listings and variants, with separate stock per branch. Receipt posting, controlled adjustments, stocktakes, transfers and quarantine actions update balances, revisions and history. Mock transfer forms select matching fixture stock and prefill quantities; Live forms require explicit choices and quantities. Drafts do not update stock. Quarantine fixtures allocate real fixture lots in expiry order and protect them from consuming movements and receipt reversal. Controlled reasons, over-quantity rejection, terminal state conflicts and same-action replay match Shop semantics. Receipt lots support expiry-aware physical availability and safe reversal; command-key replay returns the original response. Mock receiving and adjustment forms are prefilled, and mock physical-count sheets start with the expected quantity. Live count sheets remain empty until the user records a count.

Live uses the authenticated Shop inventory endpoints only. Transfer creation, dispatch and detail reads require backend access to both branches; permission failures remain visible. Permission errors, disabled writes, stale revisions and network failures remain visible failures. There is no Mock fallback. Command retries retain the same idempotency key and payload within the active workspace; an uncertain creation/adjustment locks its form for an identical retry. This is not a durable offline command queue across app restarts.

Reorder rules are read from the paginated branch rule list because Shop has no rule-by-ID GET. A failed rule read is shown separately from stock balance loading and blocks editing until it can be reloaded; it is never treated as an absent rule. Existing rules retain their returned values, including a null expiry window. Mock new-rule forms are prefilled; Live new-rule fields are empty. Mock suggestions recalculate from valid fixture stock, including quarantine holds and expiry, whenever rules are read. Alert generation is a backend worker concern; saving a rule does not imply a synchronous new alert.

Quarantine details refresh through the existing paginated branch list because Shop exposes no case-by-ID GET. Stored notes are submitted but not displayed as a returned field because the current quarantine response omits them. Generic inventory quarantine routes are separate and are not used with Shop stock-basis IDs.

The read list routes preserve pagination. Backend null arrays are valid empty lists; missing collection envelopes and malformed stock quantities are errors. Required catalogue choices that cannot load block creation instead of supplying made-up IDs.

## Contract corrections

The older Section 12B OpenAPI document omitted list query parameters and reused a broad command schema. The generator now reads the actual inventory handlers and request structs for the implemented commands. List routes include limit/offset and supported filters; receipt lines and adjustment/count/stock-basis fields use the exact source shape. Shop inventory mutations require Idempotency-Key as enforced by Shop command middleware. Backend routes were not changed.

## Remaining inventory surfaces

Reservation administration, preorder/backorder policy, fulfilment measurements, bulk imports and purchasing integrations remain separate work. Generic vendor inventory has distinct permissions and source identities; this workspace does not substitute Shop stock IDs for generic inventory IDs. Catalogue price previews still use their own returned availability contract and do not invent stock promises.
